key_insight: PI-GMDH adaptively builds the functional form of coupled physics fields during training, rather than fixing the representation upfront, and uses physics plus data residuals to guide structure growth and coefficient fitting.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to compact, accurate surrogate models for fluid dynamics when model structure, not just parameters, must be discovered from the governing equations.
method: Starts with no fixed architecture and progressively adds candidate basis functions using the first variation of the combined physical and observational objective.
Optimizes coefficients with block-coordinate damped Gauss-Newton updates after each structural expansion step.
Demonstrated on incompressible Navier-Stokes using tensor-product Chebyshev functions for the 2D time-dependent Taylor-Green vortex.
evidence_signal: On the benchmark, adaptive PI-GMDH reported validation and held-out test losses of 5.299e-19 and 5.296e-19, with 204, 201, and 175 active functions for u, v, and p.
watch_item: The comparison is explicitly presented as illustrative on a controlled synthetic benchmark, so the reported advantage may not transfer directly to harder or noisy real-world flows.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Method of Group Data Handling: Adaptive Construction of Functional Representations with an Application to the Navier-Stokes Equations
